I farm only 6 mu, so I will keep the land in the wheat-maize rotation that I know best and put the full 6.0 mu through both crops. I have 25 years of experience and well irrigation, so I will aim for stable yields instead of taking risks. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put enough nitrogen to build tillers and grain, add phosphorus and potassium to keep the stand strong, irrigate three times because wheat here depends on water at key stages, and use rotary tillage because I want a clean seedbed after maize. For summer maize, I will plant hybrid seed because I want stronger yield potential, keep fertilizer a little heavier on nitrogen, irrigate twice with my well if rainfall is not enough, and use no-tillage after wheat so I can save labor and catch the sowing window fast. I will keep pesticide use moderate on both crops because I want to control the main diseases, insects, and weeds without wasting money. My goal is steady production that fits my family labor situation and the conditions in Quzhou County.
